subject: POC trial planning —14 workload & traffic profile intake (follow-up)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning —4 next steps and intake items

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for taking the call today — good to learn more about ACME Health's use case for clinical summarization. Quick recap + recommended next steps to lock the POC: 

Summary / success criteria
- Provide 95%+ accuracy on key-entity extraction (medications, dosages, encounters) on a blinded sample of 500 de-identified notes.
- End-user latency target: median generation latency < 250ms for 512 token prompts under expected load.
- Throughput target: support steady-state 40 RPS with bursts to 120 RPS during business-hour peaks.

High-level evaluation plan
- Week 0: ingest de-identified dataset, baseline with ACME's current model.
- Week 1: Redwood deploys model variant A (quantized) and runs automated evals on the 500-note set.
- Week 2: Joint quality review and final tuning; handoff to ACME for UAT.

Ownership & timelines
- Redwood: infra + eval harness + model deployment (Ben, Marissa).
- ACME: dataset prep + legal signoff on de-id process (Sara).
- Kickoff target: next Monday 2026-03-09 if we can confirm dataset availability.

Workload intake (we need the following to size the trial and provision Dedicated capacity):
1) Expected steady-state RPS (Requests per second)
2) Typical prompt length (tokens) and expected response token lengths
3) Concurrent users / clients and any long-tail burst patterns (time-of-day)
4) Any hard SLOs for p95/p99 latency that we should target

Can you share the workload profile by end of this week? I attached a simple CSV template to collect the RPS/token data; if easier, a short reply with numbers is fine.

Attaching: redwood_poc_plan_v1.docx (outline + responsibilities) and acme_workload_profile.csv (template).

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Ben —d thanks for the recap and the templates. In-line answers below; happy to fill the CSV but sending quick numbers to unblock sizing: 

- Steady-state RPS: 35 RPS (average across the clinic hours)
- Peak burst: up to 110 RPS, typically 2-3x spikes between 08:30—10:30 PT and 13:00—14:00 PT
- Prompt length: 220 tokens (avg) — response length: 350 tokens (avg)
- Concurrency: ~25 concurrent users during peaks, but many short requests (sub-1s client-side)
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 400ms desirable; p99 < 800ms preferred for the UI team

Dataset prep: we can deliver a 500-note de-identified set by Friday 2026-03-06. Legal is looped in and okayed the de-id process (cc'd on separate thread).

Next steps: please confirm what you need for Dedicated capacity vs hosted trial — we'll likely need predictable throughput and isolation for HIPAA-sensitive logs.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Lead Platform Engineer | ACME Health
sara.patel@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning —d workload & traffic profile intake

Perfect — this is super helpful, thanks Sara. Couple quick clarifications and what we'll provision for the trial: 

Clarifications:
- When you say "prompt length 220 tokens / response 350 tokens", is that the 50th percentile or the mean? If you have 90th percentile numbers that helps sizing.
- Are the bursts short (minutes) or sustained (20—10 minutes)?

What we'll provision for POC (proposal):
- Dedicated trial pool sized for 50 RPS steady-state with headroom for short bursts to 150 RPS.
- Model variant: redwood-open-1 (8-bit quantized) deployed with KV prefix caching for repeated patient prompts.
- Autoscaling policy: scale aggressively on p95 latency > 400ms, with a short cooldown to preserve cache warmness.
- Monitoring: token-level latency and cost analytics surfaced in the Console for the trial.

Workload intake items we still need (please paste numbers or the filled CSV):
1) 50th and 90th percentile prompt lengths and response lengths (tokens)
2) Traffic distribution by hour (if you have a simple table: hour -> avg RPS)
3) Any scheduled batch jobs that will run against the model (nightly backfills)

If you can send the filled CSV by Thursday EOD (2026-03-05) we'll target onboarding on Monday 2026-03-09.

I'll ask Marissa to confirm the trial runbook and who owns each step.

-Ben

Thanks Ben & Sara — looping in the practical intake items and ownership below. See attached CSV filled with ACME's numbers (acme_workload_profile.csv) and the draft POC runbook (redwood_poc_plan_v1.docx).

POC runbook (high level)
- Day -3 (provisioning): Reserve Dedicated pool (50 RPS baseline, burst to 150 RPS), deploy redwood-open-1 quantized. Owner: Marissa Cole.
- Day 0 (ingest & baselining): Ingest de-identified 500-note dataset; run baseline eval vs ACME current. Owner: Sara / ACME.
- Day 3 (tuning): Apply prompt engineering + model param tweaks; run joint quality eval. Owner: Ben + ACME reviewers.
- Day 7 (handoff): UAT and final signoff. Owner: ACME Program Manager.

Workload profile summary (from attached CSV)
- Steady-state: 35 RPS average
- Peak bursts: 2x—3x spikes up to 110 RPS, lasting ~15—30 minutes during peak windows
- Token distribution (tokens): prompt p50=210, p90=380; response p50=340, p90=620
- Concurrency: 25 concurrent active connections on peaks; ephemeral connections otherwise
- Nightly batch: small nightly re-run of 10 RPS for nightly enrichment between 02:00—3:00 PT (will not impact production SLA)

Success criteria (confirmed)
- Entity extraction accuracy: >= 95% on blinded test set
- Latency: p95 < 400ms during steady state; p99 < 900ms during peak bursts

Next steps / action items
- Sara: share de-identified dataset (due 2026-03-06) and confirm access controls for S3 bucket.
- Marissa: provision Dedicated trial pool and share credentials (2026-03-06).
- Ben: prepare eval harness and baseline report (2026-03-09).

Attachments: acme_workload_profile.csv, redwood_poc_plan_v1.docx

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
